schemes.description: Annual UQ Ventures extracurricular challenge-based competition. Students from any faculty form (encouraged cross-disciplinary) teams at a launch panel, work over roughly a month on a themed real-world problem set with an annual partner, receive mentoring from industry mentors, and pitch solutions for prizes. Themes/partners vary by year: 2020 water scarcity with WaterStart (not-for-profit water innovation agency; 40+ teams); 2024 Ocean Innovation with the Port of Brisbane; 2026 sexual health and wellbeing with UQ SEXtember (a UQ initiative) and, per a Ventures page, ASHM.
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Teams of current UQ students from any faculty, discipline or year level
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Current UQ students; register and join a team at the first panel session (26 August in 2026).
schemes.credit_assessment: No credit; pitch competition judged against criteria provided to participants; prizes (up to $11,000 in an earlier, undated edition).
schemes.delivery_format: In person workshops/panel sessions, mentoring and final pitch
schemes.project_evidence: Teams tackle a defined annual challenge theme and pitch a solution (identifiable output: solution pitch) [1][3].
schemes.group_evidence: 'Open to teams of current UQ students'; trans-disciplinary teams formed at first panel session [1][3].
schemes.employer_evidence: Each edition has a themed partner (WaterStart 2020 [1]; Port of Brisbane 2024 [2]) and students are 'guided by industry mentors from relevant organisations' [1]. However the 2026 lead partner (UQ SEXtember) is a university initiative (internal), the external body ASHM was mentioned only on an unspecified Ventures page, and no source shows an external organisation setting a live brief, judging pitches or receiving the outputs. Theme-sponsor plus mentoring, partly internal, so Unclear.
schemes.partner_role: Theme partner (varies by year: not-for-profit, port operator, internal UQ initiative); industry mentors; judging panel composition not evidenced
schemes.named_partners: WaterStart (2020); Port of Brisbane (2024); UQ SEXtember (internal, 2026); ASHM (2026, attribution to specific page unclear)
schemes.unresolved: Whether external partners set the problem statements and sit on the judging panel; 2026 partner is internal UQ SEXtember; prize amounts for 2026 not published.

schemes.description: UQ Careers and Employability offers places on Practera's two-week virtual industry experience projects (SAIEP). Teams of international and domestic tertiary students from several Australian institutions respond to a real brief (e.g. an export brief) from an Australian or global employer in streams such as International Business, Sustainable Impact, Digital Marketing Strategy, Growth Strategy and Funding & Finance, and receive direct feedback from the client on their project outcome.

profile_md:
**University of Queensland (partial review).** The verified provision sits mainly in **Business, Economics and Law**, plus two central extracurricular routes.

- **BEL Industry Consulting Project** (RBUS3888/4888/7888, BSAN7215): selective final-year course (GPA 4.0+, by application). Project teams with an assigned mentor answer a brief from an industry partner, such as Cancer Council Queensland or Netball Queensland, and deliver a team report to the client. Applications are open for 2026-27.
- **PBEL3000 Learning by Doing in a Disruptive World:** application-only undergraduate capstone. Teams of 3-5 pitch to an industry partner, who gives feedback, and write an industry report. Last offered Summer Semester 2025.
- **MBA Impact Academy 1** (MGTS7820, 2026): teams take sponsor-set real problems and present to the sponsors. It appears to replace the MGTS7818 Industry Engagement Capstone, last evidenced in 2024. Past MBA partners include Suncorp, Anglicare and Queensland Police.
- **Central:** **Practera SAIEP** offers two-week virtual team projects for any UQ student, with briefs from real employers and client feedback. It is short and selective. The **Ventures Industry Challenge** is university-wide but only theme-partnered, and its 2026 partner is UQ's own SEXtember initiative, so criterion C is unclear.
- **Engineering/IT:** the DECO3801 team capstone uses briefs written by students. The industry-partner projects found (Data Science capstone, BE/ME placement) are individual.

No route is compulsory institution-wide; all are optional or selective. Science, HASS, law, health and architecture were **not searched** because the search budget ran out. Further routes there are likely.
gaps: Science, HASS and other faculties not searched; engineering discipline design courses not searched; Ventures Industry Challenge judging/brief role of external partners unclear; PBEL3000 2026-27 offering not confirmed; MGTS7818 status (likely replaced by Impact Academy) unconfirmed; no UQ participation numbers for Practera or BEL projects.
